summary.text: A 14-year-old boy with Down syndrome and a mental disorder had congenital atrial and ventricular septal defects and patent ductus arteriosus surgically repaired at 5 months of age, with monthly echocardiography follow-up. He was scheduled for dental treatment under general anesthesia for many dental caries. Echocardiography showed no structural problems and an ejection fraction of 85 %, his attending cardiologist categorized him as NYHA grade 1 heart failure, and the ECG showed complete right bundle branch block; vital signs and routine tests could not be obtained because he was violent.

Intramuscular midazolam 10 mg did not sedate him, so general anesthesia was induced rapidly with sevoflurane 5 % with oxygen and nitrous oxide. About 1 minute after induction his consciousness and combative behavior decreased. The ECG initially showed normal sinus rhythm with heart rate 75 bpm, then severe bradycardia below 30 bpm and asystole with no carotid pulse. Sevoflurane and nitrous oxide were stopped and CPR was started with 15 chest compressions to two ventilations.

Heartbeat and breathing returned a few minutes after CPR, an intravenous catheter was inserted, and he regained consciousness relatively early. The operation under general anesthesia was stopped. He was monitored for 1 day and discharged the next morning without sequelae. Dental treatment was later scheduled under midazolam sedation with physical restraint.
